title: A History of the Novel in Britain by Philip Hensher review – a masterpiece of criticism

paragraphs.en: In his opening paragraph, Philip Hensher declares that a novel not only “tells a good story” but is a good story in itself. We could extend that neat formula to include this book, which is not only a masterful account of fiction since 1719, when Daniel Defoe set Robinson Crusoe down on his desert island, but is itself a wonderful read. There is nothing dreary here; no sense of being back in the seminar room taking notes. Instead it is 600 pages of deep pleasure, an excuse to revisit old literary loves and be reminded of ones that have slipped from view.
paragraphs.zh: 菲利普·亨舍尔在开篇第一段就断言，一部小说不仅“讲了一个好故事”，它本身就是个好故事。我们可以把这个精妙的论断推广到这本书上：它不仅是对 1719 年丹尼尔·笛福把鲁滨逊·克鲁索放到荒岛上以来小说的权威叙述，其本身也是一本妙不可言的读物。这里毫无沉闷之感，没有回到研讨课教室里记笔记的感觉。相反，这是 600 页的深刻愉悦，是一个重温昔日文学挚爱、并记起那些从视野中滑落之作的契机。

paragraphs.en: Hensher is smart enough to know why his book works so well and vain enough to tell us. The usual methodology for a survey is to assemble a roster of academics and invite them to trot out a chapter on their specialism, whether that be “Thomas Hardy” or “High Modernism”. The result is a series of silos, with little sense of historical connection or intellectual unfolding. Hensher, by contrast, gives us a joined-up account of creative call and response. Equally crucial to this project’s success is Hensher’s own experience as a novelist. He brings a practitioner’s informed eye to such questions as why some chapters in Dickens’s Dombey and Son are in the present tense or how Henry James pulls off free indirect speech in What Maisie Knew.
paragraphs.zh: 亨舍尔聪明到足以明白自己的书为何如此成功，又自负到愿意告诉我们答案。做综述的常规做法是召集一批学者，请他们各自就自己的专长献上一章，无论是“托马斯·哈代”还是“高现代主义”。结果就是一系列彼此隔绝的孤岛，几乎没有历史联系或思想展开的感觉。相比之下，亨舍尔给我们的是一个关于创作者之间呼应关系的整体叙述。同样对这一工程的成功至关重要的，是亨舍尔本人作为小说家的经验。他以行家内行的眼光审视诸如狄更斯《董贝父子》中某些章节为何用现在时、亨利·詹姆斯如何在《梅西所知道的》中实现自由间接引语等问题。

paragraphs.en: After setting out the novel’s origin story, we are plunged into the inky churn of the middle-18th century. Samuel Richardson writes Pamela in 1740, Henry Fielding shoots back with his snarky parody, Shamela (1741), followed by the more sustained inversion of Joseph Andrews (1742). Richardson, in turn infuriated by the lack of moral purpose in Fielding’s Tom Jones (1749), storms back with The History of Sir Charles Grandison (1754).
paragraphs.zh: 在交代完小说的起源故事后，我们被抛入 18 世纪中叶的激烈纷争之中。1740 年，塞缪尔·理查逊写出了《帕梅拉》，亨利·菲尔丁随即以他尖刻的戏仿之作《沙美拉》（1741 年）回击，接着又以更系统化的反讽之作《约瑟夫·安德鲁斯》（1742 年）跟进。理查逊反过来又被菲尔丁《汤姆·琼斯》（1749 年）中道德目的的缺失激怒，便以《查尔斯·格兰迪森爵士传》（1754 年）猛烈回击。

paragraphs.en: One of the delights of Hensher’s capacious narrative is being alerted to authors and books that never got their proper due
paragraphs.zh: 亨舍尔这部容量宏大的叙事的一大乐趣，在于让你注意到那些从未得到应有评价的作家和书籍。

paragraphs.en: Hensher is brilliant on the warring duo’s finances, giving us a forensic account of the risk and reward of their different publishing models. Richardson was a printer before he was an author and hung on to his own copyrights. This allowed him the autonomy to shape the fledgling genre in ways that he wanted which, in the case of Clarissa (1748), meant 1m words written entirely in epistolary form. Fielding, no less lucky, had a patron and printer who supported him no matter how eccentric his artistic choices.
paragraphs.zh: 亨舍尔对这对宿敌的经济状况写得精彩绝伦，给我们带来了一份对二人不同出版模式风险与回报的考证式剖析。理查逊在成为作家之前是个印刷商，他一直紧握自己的版权。这让他得以按自己想要的方式塑造这个新兴文类，就《克拉丽莎》（1748 年）而言，这意味着以书信体形式写出的 100 万字。菲尔丁同样幸运，他有一位赞助人和一位印刷商，无论他的艺术选择多么古怪都支持他。

paragraphs.en: Few authors were so favoured. Jane Austen chose to sell Pride and Prejudice for a flat fee to Thomas Egerton in 1812, having previously lost money on Sense and Sensibility when she insisted on retaining copyright and paying for the printing. Under the new arrangement, Egerton was under no obligation to spend more than the minimum on production. When Pride and Prejudice eventually appeared in 1813 it was in such tiny print and scrappy paper that disgruntled readers decreed it “almost unintelligible”.
paragraphs.zh: 很少有作家如此受眷顾。1812 年，简·奥斯汀选择把《傲慢与偏见》以一次性买断的价格卖给托马斯·埃格顿，此前她在《理智与情感》上亏了钱，因为她坚持保留版权并自付印刷费。在新的安排下，埃格顿没有任何义务在制作上多花一分钱。当《傲慢与偏见》最终于 1813 年问世时，字印得极小、纸张粗糙，不满的读者判定它“几乎无法卒读”。

paragraphs.en: That sort of thing can kill a career, but Austen went on to rise above it, even if it took until the 1940s before the literary establishment caught up with her glory. One of the delights of Hensher’s capacious narrative is being alerted to authors and books that never got their proper due. Hannah More, usually written off as a Sunday school prig, turns out to be “a beautiful and graceful writer”, while Tobias Smollett, who generally gets dismissed these days as an unfunny hack, is rehabilitated as an inventive craftsman with supreme control over narrative voice. Arnold Bennett, characterised as a dreary bore thanks to Virginia Woolf’s unkind take-down of 1924, is lovingly restored as the author of the incomparable Old Wives Tale (1908), which “ought to be acknowledged among the 20 greatest novels in English”.
paragraphs.zh: 这种事足以毁掉一个人的职业生涯，但奥斯汀后来超越了它，尽管直到 20 世纪 40 年代文学界才终于认识到她的荣光。亨舍尔这部容量宏大的叙事的一大乐趣，在于让你注意到那些从未得到应有评价的作家和书籍。汉娜·莫尔通常被轻视为一个主日学校的道学先生，结果她却“是一位优美而优雅的作家”；托拜厄斯·斯莫利特如今通常被贬为一个毫无笑点的平庸写手，却被平反为一位极具创造力、对叙事声音掌控自如的工匠。由于弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫 1924 年那次不厚道的贬斥，阿诺德·本内特一直被认为是个沉闷乏味的人，如今他被深情地复原为无与伦比的《老妇谭》（1908 年）的作者，这本书“理应跻身英语世界最伟大的 20 部小说之列”。

paragraphs.en: If Hensher is generous with plaudits, he is equally vigorous in his loathing. Ann Radcliffe, author of the hugely popular and preposterously gothic The Mysteries of Udolpho (1794) “was (and remains) a simply terrible writer”. DM Thomas, Booker nominated in 1981 for The White Hotel, is “patently untalented”. And poor David Lodge, who tried so hard with modish literary pastiche in Changing Places (1975), is simply “not up to the task”.
paragraphs.zh: 如果说亨舍尔不吝赞美之词，那么他在厌恶之事上同样毫不留情。大受欢迎的荒诞哥特小说《奥多芙的神秘》（1794 年）的作者安·拉德克利夫，“（过去是，如今仍是）一个糟糕透顶的作家”。1981 年凭《白色旅馆》入围布克奖的 DM 托马斯“显然毫无才华”。还有可怜的戴维·洛奇，他在《换位》（1975 年）中如此努力地玩味时髦的文学仿作，结果“就是不堪此任”。
